sanskrit: sa tvaṃ bhrātṝn imān dṛṣṭvā pratinandasva bhārata ṛṣabhān iva saṃmattān gajendrān ūrjitān iva
english: So you, O Bhārata, looking upon these your brothers, greet them with gladness—like bulls in their prime, like mighty lordly elephants in rut.

sanskrit: amarapratimāḥ sarve śatrusāhāḥ paraṃtapāḥ eko 'pi hi sukhāyaiṣāṃ kṣamaḥ syād iti me matiḥ
english: All of them are the equals of the immortals, able to withstand any foe, scorchers of their enemies; and even one of them, I think, would suffice to bring you happiness.

sanskrit: kiṃ punaḥ puruṣavyāghrāḥ patayo me nararṣabhāḥ samastānīndriyāṇīva śarīrasya viceṣṭane
english: How much more, then, these tigers among men, my husbands, bulls among men—who are to you as all the senses together are to the body in its every action.

sanskrit: anṛtaṃ mābravīc chvaśrūḥ sarvajñā sarvadarśinī yudhiṣṭhiras tvāṃ pāñcāli sukhe dhāsyaty anuttame
english: My mother-in-law, who knew all and saw all, told me no falsehood when she said: 'O Pāñcālī, Yudhiṣṭhira shall establish you in happiness beyond compare.'

sanskrit: hatvā rājasahasrāṇi bahūny āśuparākramaḥ tad vyarthaṃ saṃprapaśyāmi mohāt tava janādhipa
english: You of swift valour, having slain many thousands of kings—yet all of that I now see made vain through your bewilderment, O lord of men.

sanskrit: yeṣām unmattako jyeṣṭhaḥ sarve tasyopacāriṇaḥ tavonmādena rājendra sonmādāḥ sarvapāṇḍavāḥ
english: Those whose eldest is crazed all follow in his train; and so, O lord of kings, through your madness all the Pāṇḍavas are stricken with madness too.

sanskrit: yadi hi syur anunmattā bhrātaras te janādhipa baddhvā tvāṃ nāstikaiḥ sārdhaṃ praśāseyur vasuṃdharām
english: For if your brothers were not maddened, O lord of men, they would bind you and, together with the unbelievers, would themselves rule the earth.

sanskrit: kurute mūḍham evaṃ hi yaḥ śreyo nādhigacchati dhūpair añjanayogaiś ca nasyakarmabhir eva ca bheṣajaiḥ sa cikitsyaḥ syād ya unmārgeṇa gacchati
english: For he who acts thus foolishly and does not attain his good is to be treated with fumigations, salves, nasal remedies, and drugs—he who walks upon a wayward path is one to be healed.

sanskrit: sāhaṃ sarvādhamā loke strīṇāṃ bharatasattama tathā vinikṛtāmitrair yāham icchāmi jīvitum
english: And so I, O best of the Bharatas, am the basest of all women in the world—I who, though our foes have been brought low, still wish to go on living.

sanskrit: eteṣāṃ yatamānānām utpadyante tu saṃpadaḥ tvaṃ tu sarvāṃ mahīṃ labdhvā kuruṣe svayam āpadam
english: To these men who strive, prosperity comes of its own accord; but you, having won the whole earth, fashion calamity for yourself.

sanskrit: yathāstāṃ saṃmatau rājñāṃ pṛthivyāṃ rājasattamau māndhātā cāmbarīṣaś ca tathā rājan virājase
english: As Māndhātṛ and Ambarīṣa, those best of kings, were honoured of kings upon the earth—so, O king, do you shine forth.

sanskrit: praśādhi pṛthivīṃ devīṃ prajā dharmeṇa pālayan saparvatavanadvīpāṃ mā rājan vimanā bhava
english: Rule the goddess Earth with her mountains, forests, and islands, guarding your subjects according to dharma; do not, O king, be downcast in spirit.

sanskrit: yajasva vividhair yajñair juhvann agnīn prayaccha ca purāṇi bhogān vāsāṃsi dvijātibhyo nṛpottama
english: Offer sacrifice with manifold rites, pouring oblations into the fires; and bestow cities, enjoyments, and garments upon the twice-born, O foremost of kings.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yājñasenyā vacaḥ śrutvā punar evārjuno 'bravīt anumānya mahābāhuṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaram īśvaram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of Yājñasenī, Arjuna again spoke, after paying due deference to his mighty-armed eldest brother, his lord.

sanskrit: daṇḍaḥ śāsti prajāḥ sarvā daṇḍa evābhirakṣati daṇḍaḥ supteṣu jāgarti daṇḍaṃ dharmaṃ vidur budhāḥ
english: The Rod of governance chastises all subjects; the Rod alone protects them; the Rod keeps watch while they sleep—the wise know the Rod to be dharma itself.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ saṃrakṣate daṇḍas tathaivārthaṃ narādhipa kāmaṃ saṃrakṣate daṇḍas trivargo daṇḍa ucyate
english: The Rod safeguards dharma, and likewise wealth, O lord of men; the Rod safeguards desire as well—the Rod is said to be the threefold aim of life.

sanskrit: daṇḍena rakṣyate dhānyaṃ dhanaṃ daṇḍena rakṣyate etad vidvann upādatsva svabhāvaṃ paśya laukikam
english: By the Rod is grain protected, by the Rod is wealth protected; grasp this, O learned one, and behold the very nature of the world.

sanskrit: rājadaṇḍabhayād eke pāpāḥ pāpaṃ na kurvate yamadaṇḍabhayād eke paralokabhayād api
english: Through fear of the king's Rod some evildoers commit no evil; some refrain through fear of Yama's rod, and some through fear of the world to come.

sanskrit: parasparabhayād eke pāpāḥ pāpaṃ na kurvate evaṃ sāṃsiddhike loke sarvaṃ daṇḍe pratiṣṭhitam
english: Through fear of one another some evildoers commit no evil; thus, in this established world, all things rest upon the Rod.

sanskrit: daṇḍasyaiva bhayād eke na khādanti parasparam andhe tamasi majjeyur yadi daṇḍo na pālayet
english: Through fear of the Rod alone some do not devour one another; men would sink into blind darkness were the Rod not to protect them.

sanskrit: yasmād adāntān damayaty aśiṣṭān daṇḍayaty api damanād daṇḍanāc caiva tasmād daṇḍaṃ vidur budhāḥ
english: Because it subdues the unsubdued and punishes the untaught—through this subduing and this punishing the wise call it the Rod, daṇḍa.

sanskrit: vāci daṇḍo brāhmaṇānāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ bhujārpaṇam dānadaṇḍaḥ smṛto vaiśyo nirdaṇḍaḥ śūdra ucyate
english: For the brāhmaṇas the rod lies in speech, for the kṣatriyas in the strength of the arm; the vaiśya's rod is reckoned to be giving, while the śūdra is said to wield no rod at all.

sanskrit: asaṃmohāya martyānām arthasaṃrakṣaṇāya ca maryādā sthāpitā loke daṇḍasaṃjñā viśāṃ pate
english: That mortals might not be confounded, and that their wealth might be preserved, the bound called the Rod was established in the world, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: yatra śyāmo lohitākṣo daṇḍaś carati sūnṛtaḥ prajās tatra na muhyanti netā cet sādhu paśyati
english: Where the dark, red-eyed Rod moves abroad in truth and justice, there the subjects are not led astray—provided the ruler sees rightly.

sanskrit: brahmacārī gṛhasthaś ca vānaprastho 'tha bhikṣukaḥ daṇḍasyaiva bhayād ete manuṣyā vartmani sthitāḥ
english: The student, the householder, the forest-dweller, and the mendicant—all these men keep to their proper path through fear of the Rod alone.

sanskrit: nābhīto yajate rājan nābhīto dātum icchati nābhītaḥ puruṣaḥ kaś cit samaye sthātum icchati
english: No man without fear offers sacrifice, O king; no fearless man wishes to give; nor does any fearless man wish to keep to his covenant.

sanskrit: nācchittvā paramarmāṇi nākṛtvā karma dāruṇam nāhatvā matsyaghātīva prāpnoti mahatīṃ śriyam
english: Without cutting into the foe's vital points, without doing terrible deeds, without slaying like a fisherman killing fish, no man wins great fortune.

sanskrit: nāghnataḥ kīrtir astīha na vittaṃ na punaḥ prajāḥ indro vṛtravadhenaiva mahendraḥ samapadyata
english: For one who does not slay there is here no glory, no wealth, nor again any subjects; it was by the killing of Vṛtra alone that Indra became the great Indra.

sanskrit: ya eva devā hantāras tāṃl loko 'rcayate bhṛśam hantā rudras tathā skandaḥ śakro 'gnir varuṇo yamaḥ
english: Those very gods who are slayers the world worships most ardently: the slayer Rudra, and Skanda, Śakra, Agni, Varuṇa, and Yama;

sanskrit: hantā kālas tathā vāyur mṛtyur vaiśravaṇo raviḥ vasavo marutaḥ sādhyā viśvedevāś ca bhārata
english: the slayer Kāla, and Vāyu, Mṛtyu, Vaiśravaṇa, and the Sun; the Vasus, the Maruts, the Sādhyas, and the Viśvedevas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: etān devān namasyanti pratāpapraṇatā janāḥ na brahmāṇaṃ na dhātāraṃ na pūṣāṇaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: To these gods the people bow, bent low before their fierce power; but to Brahmā, to Dhātṛ, to Pūṣan, never in any wise.

sanskrit: madhyasthān sarvabhūteṣu dāntāñ śamaparāyaṇān yajante mānavāḥ ke cit praśāntāḥ sarvakarmasu
english: Only a few men, themselves tranquil in all their works, worship those gods who are indifferent toward all beings, self-restrained, and devoted to peace.

sanskrit: na hi paśyāmi jīvantaṃ loke kaṃ cid ahiṃsayā sattvaiḥ sattvāni jīvanti durbalair balavattarāḥ
english: For I see no creature in the world that lives by non-injury; living beings live upon living beings, the stronger upon the weaker.

sanskrit: nakulo mūṣakān atti biḍālo nakulaṃ tathā biḍālam atti śvā rājañ śvānaṃ vyālamṛgas tathā
english: The mongoose eats mice, and the cat eats the mongoose; the dog devours the cat, O king, and the beast of prey the dog.

sanskrit: tān atti puruṣaḥ sarvān paśya dharmo yathāgataḥ prāṇasyānnam idaṃ sarvaṃ jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ ca yat
english: And man eats all of these—behold how dharma has come to be! All this, both moving and unmoving, is food for the breath of life.

sanskrit: vidhānaṃ devavihitaṃ tatra vidvān na muhyati yathā sṛṣṭo 'si rājendra tathā bhavitum arhasi
english: In this ordinance, decreed by the gods, the wise man is not bewildered; as you were created, O lord of kings, so must you consent to be.

sanskrit: vinītakrodhaharṣā hi mandā vanam upāśritāḥ vinā vadhaṃ na kurvanti tāpasāḥ prāṇayāpanam
english: For even those dull souls who, having quelled their anger and joy, have withdrawn to the forest—those ascetics cannot sustain their lives without some killing.

sanskrit: udake bahavaḥ prāṇāḥ pṛthivyāṃ ca phaleṣu ca na ca kaś cin na tān hanti kim anyat prāṇayāpanāt
english: In water are many living things, and in the earth, and in fruits; and there is no one who does not kill them—what else is this but the mere sustaining of life?

sanskrit: sūkṣmayonīni bhūtāni tarkagamyāni kāni cit pakṣmaṇo 'pi nipātena yeṣāṃ syāt skandhaparyayaḥ
english: There are beings born of subtle wombs, some apprehensible only by inference, whose mass of life might be undone by the mere falling of an eyelash.

sanskrit: grāmān niṣkramya munayo vigatakrodhamatsarāḥ vane kuṭumbadharmāṇo dṛśyante parimohitāḥ
english: Sages who have gone forth from the villages, free of anger and envy, are yet seen in the forest, deluded, keeping up the duties of a household.

sanskrit: bhūmiṃ bhittvauṣadhīś chittvā vṛkṣādīn aṇḍajān paśūn manuṣyās tanvate yajñāṃs te svargaṃ prāpnuvanti ca
english: Breaking the earth, cutting down herbs, trees, and the like, slaying egg-born creatures and beasts, men carry out their sacrifices—and so attain heaven.

sanskrit: daṇḍanītyāṃ praṇītāyāṃ sarve sidhyanty upakramāḥ kaunteya sarvabhūtānāṃ tatra me nāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: When the science of governance is rightly applied, all undertakings of every being prosper, O son of Kuntī; of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: daṇḍaś cen na bhavel loke vyanaśiṣyann imāḥ prajāḥ śūle matsyān ivāpakṣyan durbalān balavattarāḥ
english: Were there no Rod in the world, these subjects would perish; the stronger would roast the weaker as fish upon a spit.

sanskrit: satyaṃ cedaṃ brahmaṇā pūrvam uktaṃ; daṇḍaḥ prajā rakṣati sādhu nītaḥ paśyāgnayaś ca pratiśāmyanty abhītāḥ; saṃtarjitā daṇḍabhayāj jvalanti
english: And this is the truth that Brahmā spoke of old: the Rod, rightly wielded, protects the subjects. Behold—the fires die down when unafraid, but when goaded by fear of the Rod they blaze up.

sanskrit: andhaṃ tama ivedaṃ syān na prajñāyeta kiṃ cana daṇḍaś cen na bhavel loke vibhajan sādhvasādhunī
english: All this would be as blind darkness, and nothing could be discerned, were there no Rod in the world to divide the good from the wicked.

sanskrit: ye 'pi saṃbhinnamaryādā nāstikā vedanindakāḥ te 'pi bhogāya kalpante daṇḍenopanipīḍitāḥ
english: Even those who have broken every bound, the unbelievers and revilers of the Vedas, are rendered fit for enjoyment when hard pressed by the Rod.

sanskrit: sarvo daṇḍajito loko durlabho hi śucir naraḥ daṇḍasya hi bhayād bhīto bhogāyeha prakalpate
english: The whole world is governed by the Rod, for a pure man is hard to find; it is through dread, in fear of the Rod, that a man here is made fit for enjoyment.

sanskrit: cāturvarṇyāpramohāya sunītanayanāya ca daṇḍo vidhātrā vihito dharmārthāv abhirakṣitum
english: That the four orders might not fall into confusion, and that they might be led by sound policy, the Rod was ordained by the Creator to safeguard dharma and wealth.

sanskrit: yadi daṇḍān na bibhyeyur vayāṃsi śvāpadāni ca adyuḥ paśūn manuṣyāṃś ca yajñārthāni havīṃṣi ca
english: If birds and beasts of prey did not fear the Rod, they would devour the cattle and men, and the oblations meant for sacrifice.

sanskrit: na brahmacāry adhīyīta kalyāṇī gaur na duhyate na kanyodvahanaṃ gacched yadi daṇḍo na pālayet
english: No student would study, no fair cow would be milked, no maiden would be led to marriage, were the Rod not to protect us.

sanskrit: viśvalopaḥ pravarteta bhidyeran sarvasetavaḥ mamatvaṃ na prajānīyur yadi daṇḍo na pālayet
english: Universal ruin would set in, all moral boundaries would be shattered, and men would know no sense of "mine," were the Rod not to protect us.

sanskrit: na saṃvatsarasatrāṇi tiṣṭheyur akutobhayāḥ vidhivad dakṣiṇāvanti yadi daṇḍo na pālayet
english: The year-long sacrificial sessions, fearless and richly endowed with proper sacrificial fees, could not be sustained, were the Rod not to protect us.

sanskrit: careyur nāśrame dharmaṃ yathoktaṃ vidhim āśritāḥ na vidyāṃ prāpnuyāt kaś cid yadi daṇḍo na pālayet
english: Men would not follow the duty of their station as prescribed, keeping to the rule, nor would anyone attain learning, were the Rod not to protect us.

sanskrit: na coṣṭrā na balīvardā nāśvāśvataragardabhāḥ yuktā vaheyur yānāni yadi daṇḍo na pālayet
english: Neither camels nor oxen, nor horses, mules, and asses would, when yoked, draw the carriages, were the Rod not to protect us.

sanskrit: na preṣyā vacanaṃ kuryur na bālo jātu karhi cit tiṣṭhet pitṛmate dharme yadi daṇḍo na pālayet
english: Servants would not obey command, nor would a child ever abide by the duty prescribed by his father, were the Rod not to protect us.

sanskrit: daṇḍe sthitāḥ prajāḥ sarvā bhayaṃ daṇḍaṃ vidur budhāḥ daṇḍe svargo manuṣyāṇāṃ loko 'yaṃ ca pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: Upon the Rod all subjects stand; the wise know the Rod to be fear itself; upon the Rod rest both the heaven of men and this very world.

sanskrit: na tatra kūṭaṃ pāpaṃ vā vañcanā vāpi dṛṣyate yatra daṇḍaḥ suvihitaś caraty arivināśanaḥ
english: There no deceit, no evil, nor any fraud is seen, where the Rod, well-ordained and destroyer of foes, walks abroad.

sanskrit: haviḥ śvā prapibed dhṛṣṭo daṇḍaś cen nodyato bhavet haret kākaḥ puroḍāśaṃ yadi daṇḍo na pālayet
english: The dog would boldly lap up the oblation were the Rod not held aloft; the crow would carry off the sacrificial cake, were the Rod not to protect us.

sanskrit: yad idaṃ dharmato rājyaṃ vihitaṃ yady adharmataḥ kāryas tatra na śoko vai bhuṅkṣva bhogān yajasva ca
english: Whether this kingship has been ordained righteously or unrighteously, no grief should be felt over it; enjoy your pleasures and offer sacrifice.

sanskrit: sukhena dharmaṃ śrīmantaś caranti śucivāsasaḥ saṃvasantaḥ priyair dārair bhuñjānāś cānnam uttamam
english: The prosperous, clad in clean raiment, dwelling with their beloved wives and eating the finest food, practise dharma in ease.

sanskrit: arthe sarve samārambhāḥ samāyattā na saṃśayaḥ sa ca daṇḍe samāyattaḥ paśya daṇḍasya gauravam
english: Upon wealth all undertakings depend, without doubt; and wealth itself depends upon the Rod—behold the greatness of the Rod!

sanskrit: lokayātrārtham eveha dharmapravacanaṃ kṛtam ahiṃsā sādhuhiṃseti śreyān dharmaparigrahaḥ
english: It is for the sake of the world's course that the teaching of dharma was made here. "Non-injury" and "the slaying of the wicked is righteous slaying"—of these, the wider embrace of dharma is the better.

sanskrit: nātyantaguṇavān kaś cin na cāpy atyantanirguṇaḥ ubhayaṃ sarvakāryeṣu dṛśyate sādhv asādhu ca
english: No one is wholly endowed with virtue, nor is anyone wholly devoid of it; in all actions both are seen—the good and the bad alike.

sanskrit: paśūnāṃ vṛṣaṇaṃ chittvā tato bhindanti nastakān kṛṣanti bahavo bhārān badhnanti damayanti ca
english: Men geld the cattle and then pierce their nostrils; many drag heavy loads, and they bind the beasts and break them in.

sanskrit: evaṃ paryākule loke vipathe jarjarīkṛte tais tair nyāyair mahārāja purāṇaṃ dharmam ācara
english: In a world thus thrown into turmoil, gone astray and worn to tatters, practise the ancient dharma, O great king, by those very rules of conduct.

sanskrit: yaja dehi prajā rakṣa dharmaṃ samanupālaya amitrāñ jahi kaunteya mitrāṇi paripālaya
english: Sacrifice, give, protect your subjects, and uphold dharma; slay your enemies, O son of Kuntī, and cherish your friends.

sanskrit: mā ca te nighnataḥ śatrūn manyur bhavatu bhārata na tatra kilbiṣaṃ kiṃ cit kartur bhavati bhārata
english: And let there be no anguish in you when you slay your foes, O Bhārata; in that there is no sin at all for the doer, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ātatāyī hi yo hanyād ātatāyinam āgatam na tena bhrūṇahā sa syān manyus taṃ manyum ṛcchati
english: For he who slays an oncoming assailant bent on murder does not by that become a slayer of the unborn; rather, the assailant's own fury recoils upon his fury.

sanskrit: avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānām antarātmā na saṃśayaḥ avadhye cātmani kathaṃ vadhyo bhavati kena cit
english: The inmost Self of all beings cannot be slain—of this there is no doubt; and if the Self cannot be slain, how can anyone be slain by any means?

sanskrit: yathā hi puruṣaḥ śālāṃ punaḥ saṃpraviśen navām evaṃ jīvaḥ śarīrāṇi tāni tāni prapadyate
english: For just as a man might enter again into a new house, so does the living soul pass into one body after another.

sanskrit: dehān purāṇān utsṛjya navān saṃpratipadyate evaṃ mṛtyumukhaṃ prāhur ye janās tattvadarśinaḥ
english: Casting off its old bodies, it takes on new ones; thus do those men who perceive the truth speak of the gateway of death.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca arjunasya vacaḥ śrutvā bhīmaseno 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ dhairyam āsthāya tejasvī jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaram abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of Arjuna, Bhīmasena, hard to provoke yet now stirred, the resplendent one, summoning his firmness, spoke to his eldest brother.

sanskrit: rājan viditadharmo 'si na te 'sty aviditaṃ bhuvi upaśikṣāma te vṛttaṃ sadaiva na ca śaknumaḥ
english: O king, you know what dharma is; there is nothing upon earth unknown to you. We ever strive to learn your conduct, yet we are not able to.

sanskrit: na vakṣyāmi na vakṣyāmīty evaṃ me manasi sthitam atiduḥkhāt tu vakṣyāmi tan nibodha janādhipa
english: "I will not speak, I will not speak"—thus it was fixed in my mind; yet out of overwhelming grief I shall speak. Hear it then, O lord of men.

sanskrit: bhavatas tu pramohena sarvaṃ saṃśayitaṃ kṛtam viklavatvaṃ ca naḥ prāptam abalatvaṃ tathaiva ca
english: By your bewilderment all has been thrown into doubt; faintness of heart has come upon us, and weakness as well.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi rājā lokasya sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ moham āpadyate dainyād yathā kupuruṣas tathā
english: How is it that a king of the world, skilled in all the treatises, falls into delusion out of dejection, like some base man?

sanskrit: āgatiś ca gatiś caiva lokasya viditā tava āyatyāṃ ca tadātve ca na te 'sty aviditaṃ prabho
english: The coming and going of the world are known to you; in things to come and in the present moment alike, there is nothing unknown to you, O lord.

sanskrit: evaṃ gate mahārāja rājyaṃ prati janādhipa hetum atra pravakṣyāmi tad ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu
english: This being so, O great king, lord of men, concerning the kingdom I shall now declare the reason; hear it here with single-minded attention.

sanskrit: dvividho jāyate vyādhiḥ śārīro mānasas tathā parasparaṃ tayor janma nirdvaṃdvaṃ nopalabhyate
english: Disease arises of two kinds, the bodily and the mental; their origins are bound to each other, and neither is found to arise free of the other.

sanskrit: śārīrāj jāyate vyādhir mānaso nātra saṃśayaḥ mānasāj jāyate vyādhiḥ śārīra iti niścayaḥ
english: From the bodily arises the mental disease—of this there is no doubt; and from the mental arises the bodily: such is the settled conclusion.
